title: BYOK onboarding checklist and SIEM mapping
content:
Purpose:
This working doc consolidates the pragmatic onboarding checklist for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) customers, maps the audit log schema to SIEM events, and proposes RBAC v2 role mappings for key operations. Goal is to produce a testable acceptance matrix and a minimal evidence automation plan we can hand to SRE/DevOps for implementation.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: security, solutions eng, infra, SRE, and customer onboarding engineers.
- Scope: KMS/HSM integration patterns, BYOK onboarding steps, scheduled + emergency rotation procedures, RBAC v2 role obligations for key lifecycle operations, and SIEM export mapping for evidence and alerts. Not covering billing, contract/legal language, or on-prem appliance procurement logistics (separate doc).

High-level constraints and assumptions:
- We assume customers will use either cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) or an external HSM provider that supports PKCS#11 or AWS CloudHSM-style flows.
- Private deployments use same control plane but customer-managed networking; we will not ship key material into our control plane for BYOK unless explicitly agreed.
- All audit events must be cryptographically tamper-evident and exportable to Splunk/Datadog/Microsoft Sentinel via our SIEM export pipeline.

Quick summary of deliverables from this doc (unchecked means TODO):
- [x] BYOK onboarding checklist (operational steps + test vectors)
- [x] RBAC v2 role mapping for key ops (read/write/rotate/escrow)
- [x] Audit event schema (canonical field names)
- [ ] SIEM mapping table (field -> Splunk sourcetype/Datadog facet)
- [ ] Evidence automation prototype (lambda + pipeline)
- [ ] Acceptance test matrix for customer onboarding (SLOs, latency, artifact generation)

1) BYOK onboarding checklist (step-by-step, runbook style)
- Pre-engagement: legal/contract sign-off (customer agrees to BYOK responsibilities); collect contact and operational SLAs. (owner: sales/solutions)
- Security review call: confirm HSM vendor, key usage policy (sign/encrypt/decrypt), supported algorithms, and key expiry/rotation cadence. (owner: sec-eng)
- Network readiness: confirm VPC peering, firewall rules, certs, and routing for private-control-plane to customer KMS endpoint. For on-prem HSMs confirm VPN/Bastion access. (owner: infra)
- RBAC provisioning: map customer admin(s) to RBAC v2 roles (see section 3).
- Key escrow policy: confirm whether escrow is required. If yes, define escrow storage, split-knowledge, and recovery process.
- Test keys: customer to create test key(s) with same properties; provide ephemeral key IDs.
- Integration test: perform a sequence of signed calls: CreateKeyMetadata -> Encrypt(sample) -> Decrypt(sample) -> Sign(sample) -> Verify(sample). Capture logs.
- Rotation rehearsal: perform a non-production key rotation and validate that existing ciphertext can still be decrypted using key versions or rewrap process.
- Evidence package: produce artifacts (audit logs, key version table, TLS session logs, network flow summary) and deliver to customer & internal compliance.
- Go-live signoff: operations checklist complete and customer approves.

Notes: include short commands/snippets for engineers (kept informal):
- AWS example (pseudo): aws kms generate-data-key --key-id alias/customer-byok --key-spec AES_256 --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > enc_blob.bin
- HSM example: use pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/your-hsm.so --login --pin XXXX --sign --input data.bin --output sig.bin

2) RBAC v2 role mapping (proposal)
We want least-privilege, auditable roles that map to key lifecycles. Keep role names short; align with product RBAC primitives.
- role:key-admin (can create/delete/manage key metadata, rotate keys, set usage policy, request escrow)
- role:key-operator (can perform runtime operations: encrypt, decrypt, sign, rewrap; cannot change metadata/rotation schedule)
- role:key-auditor (read-only: view key metadata, versions, and audit trails; cannot request crypto ops)
- role:key-recovery (can perform key-recovery/escrow retrieval under documented emergency process; requires dual-approval)
- role:key-infra (SRE-level: manage connectors, rotation jobs, and SIEM pipelines, but cannot access plaintext key material)

RBAC enforcement notes:
- All privileged ops (rotate, escrow retrieve) must require a 2-person approval workflow logged in audit.
- Token exchange for runtime servers should use short-lived credentials and be bound to a service identity that maps to role:key-operator.

3) Key rotation procedure (normal cadence + emergency)
Normal rotation (recommended):
- Frequency: customer-defined; default recommended: 90 days for symmetric data keys, 365 days for master KEKs.
- Mechanism: perform a versioned rotation where new key version is created and set as primary; older versions kept for decryption until TTL expires (replay window).
- Rewrap path: if ciphertext contains key version info, rewrap or re-encrypt at next opportunity during read path. Provide background migration job that re-encrypts hot objects within 7 days of rotation.
- Post-rotation validation: run decrypt of a token set (N=100 sample objects) and verify logs and SIEM events produced.

Emergency rotation (compromise suspected):
- Trigger: detected QPS anomalies, unauthorized key access event, or HSM breach notification.
- Immediate actions: mark compromised key as disabled (deny new encrypt/sign), create replacement key version, update routing/policies to use replacement.
- For long-lived ciphertext where rewrap is infeasible, use dual-read logic in service: when decrypting, if primary fails try secondary with alerting.
- Evidence preservation: snapshot HSM audit logs, export KMS event history, preserve network captures for forensics (follow legal hold).

4) Audit log schema (canonical fields for all key events)
We must unify events across cloud KMS and HSM. Canonical field names below are the target fields our ingestion pipeline will normalize.
- event_ts (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (UUID)
- actor_type (user|service|system)
- actor_id (email/service-id)
- action (create-key|encrypt|decrypt|sign|verify|rotate|disable|enable|escrow-request|escrow-grant|export-audit|attach-policy)
- key_id (the canonical key identifier we use in control plane)
- key_version (v1,v2...)
- algorithm (RSA-2048, RSA-3072, EC-P256, AES-256-GCM, etc)
- status (success|failure|denied|warning)
- error_code (if failure)
- client_ip
- tls_cipher
- request_id (upstream request tracker)
- session_id
- audit_hash (hash of canonical JSON event for tamper-evidence)
- raw_provider_event (small blob or reference id to raw cloud provider record)
- extra (freeform text)

5) SIEM export mapping and alerting (notes, TODO)
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON with canonical fields. Use gzip + HTTP ingestion to the SIEM.
- Suggested sourcetype/tags: key-event, byok, encrypted-ops, rotation.
- Example alert rules:
  - high-priority: "unauthorized decrypt" -> event.action==decrypt && event.status==denied && actor_type==user -> PagerDuty
  - medium: "mass rotate" -> sudden >10 rotations in 1 minute -> Slack ops-channel + ticket creation
  - forensic: "escrow retrieval" -> escrow-grant events should generate an immutable evidence bundle and require approval ID in event.extra

Mapping TODO: complete splunk sourcetype and Datadog facet names. (owner: observability team, target: 2 sprints)

6) Evidence automation sketch (artifact types + retention)
Artifacts to collect for each critical operation (create, rotate, escrow, emergency-rotation):
- canonical event JSONs (signed with audit key)
- HSM audit log exports (PKCS#11 session logs, sequence numbers)
- Key version table (CSV snapshot)
- TLS session logs for the control plane call (cert fingerprint, cipher)
- Network flow summary (5-tuple) for the session window
- Two-person approval records (IDs of approvers and timestamp)
Retention and access: store artifacts in encrypted S3 with KMS envelope (access restricted to role:key-auditor + legal for eDiscovery). Retention defaults: 7 years for master key ops evidence unless customer requests shorter.

Automation prototype idea:
- lambda/audit-ingester reads normalized events -> signs event with internal audit key -> uploads event and index into evidence-bucket -> triggers evidence-builder job that collects provider raw logs and assembles zip + manifest -> push to SIEM and to escrow bucket if request is for escrow.
- Access to evidence-bucket gated by KMS policy and IAM roles; retrieval requires dual-approval workflow.

7) Acceptance test matrix (high level)
Columns: test-case, input, expected-output, audit-events, SIEM-alert, owner. Example rows (informal):
- Key create end-to-end: create test key -> kms returns key-id -> audit event create-key present with audit_hash -> SIEM receives event within 30s -> status PASS
- Encrypt/Decrypt: encrypt sample -> decrypt sample -> result matches plaintext -> two audit events encrypt+decrypt with same request_id -> SIEM alert none -> PASS
- Rotation normal: rotate key in staging -> new key version present, background rewrap job re-encrypts sample within 7 days -> audit event rotate + rewrap events present -> PASS

8) Open questions / risks / decisions needed
- Do we allow any mode where customer uploads raw key material into our control plane? (default: no; accept only under strict escrow agreements)
- Escrow policy: who pays for long-term escrow storage? Pricing impact TBD.
- Legal holds & cross-border: need to decide whether evidence exports cross region by default.
- SIEM normalization: what cardinality limits should we enforce for 'extra' field?

Next steps (practical):
- Obs team: produce SIEM sourcetype mapping doc (2 weeks).
- SRE/infra: prototype evidence-ingester lambda (3 sprints).
- Security: finalize RBAC v2 policy docs and 2-person workflow integration with IDP (1 sprint).
- Solutions eng: create customer-ready BYOK onboarding checklist (this doc -> cleaned + add checkboxes) and a sample test harness repo.

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Confluence + Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Key+Management+Overview
- Jira epic: SEC-5123 (BYOK + Evidence Automation)
- TODO: add example Splunk queries and Datadog dashboards here (placeholder)

Notes to self: doc is intentionally practical — avoid re-stating KMS vendor docs; capture operational edge cases (rekey vs rewrap, token migration windows, how to handle long-tail ciphertext). Keep this doc as the single living onboarding checklist until we split into formal runbook + engineering tickets.

-- Priya (initial draft)
